metric.capability_efficiency.basis: all-fragments (Python-only shard; common-basis figure requires merge with the other nine language shards by the runner before a comparability gate can be evaluated)
metric.capability_efficiency.basis_size_note: This shard covers all 44 frozen probes for Python. It cannot itself determine which probes fall in the 10-language common basis; that determination is deferred to the runner's merge step per spec 6.1.4 interaction_with_quality_metrics.

capability_efficiency_normalized.caveat: This shard evaluates Python only and has no visibility into the other nine languages' raw capability_efficiency figures. Per spec 6.1.4/6.1.5, normalized scores are comparative (higher = better across the fixed 10-language column order) and the common-basis figure additionally requires the runner to intersect this language's supported-probe set with the other nine languages' supported-probe sets before A-D/E are computed on the common basis. The value reported here is a self-contained monotonic transform of the raw figure (100/(1+raw), which preserves 'lower raw = higher score, higher = better, bounded in (0,100)') and is offered so this work unit is independently scoreable per spec 'unfinished applicable work is not N/A'. The runner must recompute the final normalized and common-basis figures once all ten language shards for metric.capability_efficiency are merged, using raw_totals.total_complexity_units and raw_totals.supported_capability_points published here as the frozen raw inputs.

capability_efficiency_raw.interpretation: 2.373 semantic-complexity units required per supported capability point for Python, on the all-fragments basis.

frozen_counting_rule.context_dependent_rules: Count of frozen semantic_facts_expected for the probe whose correct interpretation depends on information outside the measured_fragment's local syntax (e.g. dynamic name resolution, duck-typed dispatch resolved only at the call target, non-enforced conventions such as leading-underscore privacy or ALL_CAPS constants) per Python Language Reference chapters 3 (data model) and 4 (execution model).
frozen_counting_rule.documented_semantic_exceptions: Count of named departures from a general rule that Python's own reference/documentation states explicitly for the constructs used (e.g. floor-division/modulo sign rule in the Reference's 'Binary arithmetic operations' section, UnboundLocalError as an exception to normal name binding, `__del__` non-guaranteed timing documented in the Data Model chapter, absence of checked exceptions as a documented departure from other languages' propagation model).
frozen_counting_rule.implicit_rules: Count of behaviors that occur at the fragment's site without a corresponding local written marker (implicit numeric promotion, implicit pass-by-object-reference, implicit exception propagation with no declared checked-exception surface, implicit refcounting-based cleanup, arbitrary-precision integers implicitly suppressing overflow) per Python Language Reference chapters 3, 6 and the `sys`/`gc` documentation.
frozen_counting_rule.purpose: Per semantic_compression.md section 6.1.4.E and 20, the counting rule for each complexity sub-category is frozen BEFORE annotation and itemised so the figure is auditable. All four sub-categories below are governed by an observable rule grounded in the Python Language Reference / Python documentation, so none is recorded as 'unknown'.
frozen_counting_rule.syntax_forms: Count of distinct Python grammatical construct KINDS (statement or expression forms, e.g. assignment-statement, if/else, def, with-statement, try/except, subscript, slice, call-expression, comprehension) required inside the measured_fragment to deliver the canonical_task, per R5. Two uses of the same construct kind count once.

gates.scoreability_note: This figure is reported as unfinished-but-scoreable raw+provisional evidence per primary.json scoreability.unfinished_applicable_work_is_not_na; it is not a genuine N/A because measurement was taken for every one of the 44 frozen probes for the assigned language.

per_probe_support_and_complexity.reason: Python has no syntax for a non-reassignable local binding; ordinary assignment is used and reassignment is never rejected by the language.
Module-level mutable storage is native; the 'constant' is only a naming convention (UPPER_CASE), not enforced.
Python has no declaration-without-initializer statement; name binding only occurs at assignment. UnboundLocalError is the documented exception mechanism if a path misses assignment.
Named R9 substitution: Python's bytearray(16) is documented as zero-initialized, not genuinely uninitialized; substitute fragment written per rule.

per_probe_support_and_complexity.note: x += 1; arbitrary-precision int implicitly removes overflow concerns.
xs[1] = 42; in-place mutation of the list object.

per_probe_support_and_complexity.reason: Python has no documented mechanism for two names in one scope to share writable scalar storage; ints are immutable and there is no reference/pointer type for locals. (Language Reference ch.3: 'Data model'.)
A second name bound to the same list object is not a distinct read-only view type; read-only-ness is unenforced.

per_probe_support_and_complexity.note: list.append/pop round-trip plus `is` identity test.
Bare call f(x): pass-by-object-reference is implicit and not locally distinguishable from copy semantics.

per_probe_support_and_complexity.reason: No documented mechanism for a callee to write a caller's scalar local; ints are immutable and Python has no inout/reference parameter form. Rubric explicitly excludes a mutable-container wrapper as an acceptable FULL substitute.

per_probe_support_and_complexity.note: def + map(); documented late-binding-closure exception for captured names.
tuple literal + unpacking.
//, %, / ; documented floor-division/negative-modulo sign rule.

per_probe_support_and_complexity.reason: Python ints are arbitrary-precision; a genuinely fixed-width overflow site requires the stdlib ctypes.c_int32 wrapping type, which is a non-idiomatic escape hatch.

per_probe_support_and_complexity.note: explicit `if b == 0` guard around ordinary `/`/`//`.
`==` dispatches to `__eq__`, documented content comparison for str.
sorted(xs, reverse=True) returns a new list; `<` operator.

per_probe_support_and_complexity.reason: No native 32/64-bit int distinction; narrowing with a documented out-of-range signal requires ctypes.c_int32.

per_probe_support_and_complexity.note: `i + d`; numeric tower implicit int-to-float promotion.
xs[i] raises documented IndexError.
xs[1:4]; list slicing is documented to copy.

per_probe_support_and_complexity.reason: Named R9 substitution: no enforced Optional type or coalescing operator; conditional expression used as the standard fallback form.
Named R9 substitution: no optional-aware chaining operator; explicit conditional written.

per_probe_support_and_complexity.note: int(s) raises ValueError; Python has no checked-exception declaration, documented departure from checked-exception languages.
try/except ValueError.

per_probe_support_and_complexity.reason: Named R9 substitution: no closed sum type; nearest standard form is an open class hierarchy or Enum-tagged dataclass, not closed by language rule.
if/elif isinstance dispatch has no compiler-checked exhaustiveness guarantee.

per_probe_support_and_complexity.note: Duck-typed extension from a separate module is native and unrestricted.

per_probe_support_and_complexity.reason: Named R9 substitution: Python generics (typing.TypeVar) are unenforced annotations; the runtime relies on duck typing, not a checked type-parameter relationship.

Named R9 substitution: declaration-site constraint (typing.Protocol bound) is not enforced at the declaration; misuse is only diagnosed, if at all, by an optional external type checker not run under the frozen recipe.

per_probe_support_and_complexity.note: Heterogeneous list plus duck-typed dispatch is native.
list literal + sum().
dict literal, .values(), .get(key, default) documented lookup-with-default.
`with open(...) as f:` context-manager protocol guarantees __exit__ on every path.

per_probe_support_and_complexity.reason: __del__ end-of-lifetime hook timing is documented as not guaranteed by the language (only conventional in CPython's refcounting implementation).

per_probe_support_and_complexity.note: print("x") is a builtin, no import required.

per_probe_support_and_complexity.reason: Leading-underscore 'privacy' is a documented convention, not an enforced access boundary.

per_probe_support_and_complexity.note: asyncio.gather + asyncio.run is the stdlib async facility shipped with the frozen recipe.
threading.Thread + threading.Lock documented to make the guarded increment race-free.
ctypes.CDLL is the stdlib FFI mechanism shipped with the frozen toolchain.

per_probe_support_and_complexity.reason: `python3 FILE.py` under the frozen recipe produces no compiled artifact with an exported unmangled C symbol; N-1 per rubric, `nm` field records 'no compiled artifact under the frozen recipe'.

raw_totals.supported_capability_points_formula: sum over 44 probes of capability_points(2) * support_factor; FULL=1, PARTIAL=0.5, NONE=0 => 26*2 + 15*1 + 3*0 = 67
raw_totals.total_complexity_units_formula: sum of (syntax_forms + context_dependent_rules + implicit_rules + documented_semantic_exceptions) over every probe with support in {FULL, PARTIAL}; NONE probes contribute 0 because no fragment exists to measure (per spec 6.1.4.E and na_policy NA-2/NA-4).

semantic_regularity_evidence_used_for_th.note: Per spec section 20, the exception/context/implicit counts above double as this probe-set's contribution to Rule Exception Density evidence and are not separately re-derived; they are drawn once from the same itemised per-probe table and are not double counted across Hidden Semantic Cost and Capability Efficiency beyond what each metric's own definition requires.

metric.capability_efficiency.support_rubric_application_note: Support level (FULL/PARTIAL/NONE) for each probe was assigned using the frozen deterministic_tie_break question from capability_universe.json support_rubric, applied to documented Python 3 standard-library capability under the frozen recipe (python3 FILE.py, stdlib only, no third-party packages). NONE fragments carry a documented citation and contribute 0 to both the complexity numerator and the coverage numerator (NA-2); their capability_points still count in the fixed 88-point Capability Coverage denominator but are irrelevant to this Efficiency metric's numerator/denominator, which use only the supported-points total.
